column1: # G4 phase 4: the aontu:system VOCABULARY
# (docs/capability-review/g4-identity-relations.md). Ports, components
# and relations need no syntax: they are schemas. Everything in
# `@"aontu:system"` is ordinary unification -- conjunction, spreads,
# marks, defaults -- so the vocabulary costs the language nothing, and
# an author who wants a different one writes it the same way.
# The source is BUNDLED with the engine (the aontu/ tree, ADR-036): no
# filesystem, no package resolution, so it is available under every
# include capability except `none`, and the hermeticity posture is not
# widened by a source that never leaves the process. The two copies are
# the same bytes, and `vocabulary-canon` and `vocabulary-hash` below pin
# that in both engines -- they cannot drift without a red suite.
# EXPERIMENTAL until the distribution layer can version it by
# canon-hash.
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md).
vocabulary-is-served
# THE SCHEME IS NOT A DIRECTORY (ADR-028): the `.aontu` spelling the
# bare `std/` names once accepted is not a model name, and is
# refused like any other typo, as aontu-scheme.tsv pins for
# `aontu:profile.aontu`.

# expecting `"sideways"` to pass): a preferred member no longer holds
# the disjunction open, so `*in | out | inout` is a true
# enum-with-default -- unset generates `in`, `out`/`inout` override,
# anything else is the `empty` refusal. The old row recorded the
# fail-open behaviour of use-cases/BUGS.md §1. Parity-probed.

component-ports-are-ports
component-ports-take-the-port-default
component-without-ports

service-kind-is-fixed
# The Relation schema is GONE (RELATIONS.0.md P2): a relation is
# declared by the graph atoms at its field -- `rel(t) & acyclic() &
# inverse(name)` -- so `target` is rel(t)'s flow and the other two are
# the atoms, all pinned in test/spec/relation.tsv. A document still
# reaching for the old member gets the ordinary missing-path refusal.
relation-schema-retired
# The design's own figure, evaluated: identified services, a typed

# (rel + the graph atoms), with the mirror the inverse asks for
# written out. The graph row is what the verdict consumes.
the-worked-example

# SEMVER (semver.org 2.0.0) --- an ORDERED TUPLE: major, minor, patch,
# pre-release, build. A list and not a dotted string, because a version
# is COMPARED and the comparison runs component by component from the
# left: "1.10.0" sorts below "1.9.0" as text. A list and not a map,
# because a map has no order of its own to compare along.
# THE TAIL DEFAULTS. [1] is [1 0 0 "" ""] and [1 2] is [1 2 0 "" ""]: a
# major-only version is the common case and costs one token.
semver-major-only
semver-major-minor
semver-triple
semver-zero
semver-prerelease
semver-build
semver-prerelease-and-build
# A SIXTH ELEMENT IS NOT PART OF A VERSION: the arity is bounded, and
# the bound is checked after the defaults fill.
semver-too-long
# The numeric parts are non-negative integers. LEADING ZEROES need no
# rule there: 01 is not a distinct integer literal, so the spec's "MUST
# NOT contain leading zeroes" is impossible to write rather than merely
# forbidden.
semver-negative-refused
semver-non-integer-refused
# THE PRE-RELEASE IS CHECKED BY GRAMMAR, structure and alphabet both.
# An alphabet pattern could not do this: the spec's shape is
# dot-separated identifiers, which as a regex is a quantified group
# containing a quantifier -- refused outright by re() for backtracking
# exponentially (constraint_pattern). The ABNF in the vocabulary says
# it directly, so the empty identifier and the leading zero are caught
# where the pattern let them through.
semver-prerelease-alphabet
semver-prerelease-empty-identifier
semver-prerelease-leading-zero
# ...and only where the spec forbids it: an identifier that is not
# wholly numeric may start with a zero.
semver-prerelease-alphanumeric-zero
# BUILD METADATA has its own grammar, and it is not the pre-release
# one: the spec allows a leading zero here, because build metadata is
# never compared.
semver-build-leading-zero
semver-build-alphabet
# The dotted STRING is not a version here, which is the whole point of
# the list: it never enters the model as text that sorts wrong.
semver-string-refused
